headline: A Sunday letter about the panic
summary: On a quiet Sunday Roosevelt writes his friend and physician Dr. Alexander Lambert about the financial panic gripping the country.

events.detail: Writes Dr. Lambert about the financial crisis

letters.topic: The Panic of 1907

headline: Anniversary gift as Congress convenes
summary: On their 21st wedding anniversary Edith gives Roosevelt Izaak Walton's The Compleat Angler, a gift he treasures. The 60th Congress opens, and he spends the day on currency and railroad law with senators, plays tennis with Jusserand and Pinchot, then laughs his way through the comedy Brewster's Millions.

Talks currency legislation with Senator Hansbrough
Talks Interstate Commerce Act changes with Cooper

Tennis with the French ambassador, Pinchot and Smith
Evening at the theater with Edith to see Brewster's Millions

letters.topic: Physical fitness tests for Army officers
A postmaster's job in Dallas, Texas

headline: Annual Message calls for income tax
summary: Roosevelt's Annual Message goes to Congress, pressing for reform and proposing both an inheritance tax and an income tax. A congressional committee calls to report the session open, the Cabinet meets, and he walks with Jusserand and Winthrop before an evening on finance bills with Aldrich and Crane.

events.detail: A congressional committee formally tells him Congress has convened
His Annual Message, urging inheritance and income taxes, is read to Congress
Walk with Jusserand and Beekman Winthrop
Evening talk on finance bills with Aldrich and Crane

uncertain: Edith's letter to Kermit about the anniversary is noted but is not TR's; omitted from letters.

headline: A rebuke for Puerto Rico's governor
summary: Roosevelt sees Lodge and a line of other callers, receives German Ambassador von Sternberg at five, and takes an afternoon walk. By letter he scolds Puerto Rico's governor, Regis Post, for careless public remarks.

events.detail: Callers include Lodge, Senator George C. Perkins and General Clayton

letters.topic: Reprimand over his unwise public comments

headline: Brander Matthews comes to stay
summary: Governor Cummins, naturalist C. Hart Merriam and Dr. Rixey join Roosevelt for lunch, and more lawmakers call. After a ride he dines with Columbia professor Brander Matthews and Yale's Thomas Lounsbury, who both spend the night at the White House.

events.detail: Lunch guests include Iowa's governor and Dr. Rixey
Congressmen and New York's William Barnes call
Brander Matthews and Lounsbury dine and stay overnight

uncertain: The record lists two lunches with overlapping guests; they are treated as one. Lounsbury is taken to be Thomas R. Lounsbury of Yale.

headline: Federal troops ordered to Nevada
summary: With Nevada's gold camps sliding toward lawlessness, Governor John Sparks asks for help and Roosevelt sends Army troops under General Funston. He also tours the Corcoran with Brander Matthews, plays tennis, and dines with friends from his Louisiana bear hunt.

events.detail: Labor unrest erupts in Nevada's gold mining districts
Morning visit to the Corcoran Gallery with Brander Matthews
Callers include Kellogg, Frye, Clapp and McLaurin
Dinner with companions from the Louisiana hunting trip

headline: A bird refuge for Louisiana
summary: Roosevelt sets aside East Timbalier Island in Louisiana as a bird reservation. He greets the ambassadors of Mexico, Italy and Britain, lunches with Captains Lee and McCoy and a Mr. Sargent, and rides. Mrs. J. West Roosevelt is staying at the White House.

events.detail: Callers include Townsend, Gardner, Governor Smith, Metcalf and Cockrell
Receives the ambassadors of Italy, Britain and Mexico
Lunch with two Army captains and Sargent

East Timbalier Island Bird Reservation established

letters.topic: Political strife in New Mexico

uncertain: The record gives only the surname; Sargent may be the painter John Singer Sargent.

headline: Evening callers on a Sunday
summary: A quiet Sunday ends with two evening visitors: Representative Fassett at nine, then diplomat William Rockhill half an hour later.

headline: A loving cup for Trevelyan
summary: Roosevelt meets a long list of lawmakers along with labor leader Samuel Gompers, and lunches with Thomas Watson, Cortelyou and Straus. He tells historian George Otto Trevelyan that he, Lodge and Root are sending a silver loving cup to honor his books on the American Revolution.

events.detail: Callers include Fairbanks, Hepburn, Gompers and Charles P. Neill
Lunch with Watson and cabinet members
Writes Trevelyan about a gift cup from himself, Lodge and Root

letters.topic: A silver cup honoring his histories of the Revolution

uncertain: Thomas Watson identified as Thomas E. Watson, the Georgia Populist, by context of later greenback letter; not certain.

headline: Lunch with Ambassador Bryce
summary: After the Cabinet meets and a few congressmen call, Roosevelt lunches with British Ambassador James Bryce and Secretary Root, plays tennis with Garfield, Cooley and Jusserand, and dines at Lodge's.

events.detail: Lunch with the British ambassador and Root

headline: Conservation allies at day's end
summary: Roosevelt sees John Sharp Williams, Bonaparte and Meyer among the day's callers, lunches with his son-in-law Nick Longworth and others, rides, and closes the afternoon with Garfield, Pinchot and Beveridge.

events.detail: Callers include J. S. Williams, Bonaparte, Meyer and Hitchcock
Lunch with Pritchett, Longworth and others

headline: No third term, Roosevelt declares
summary: Roosevelt makes it public: he will not seek a third term as President, and he writes Taft about the statement. Between meetings on California appointments and lunch with Hoke Smith and Frank Kellogg, he still finds time for tennis with Garfield, Jusserand and Cooley.

events.detail: Discusses appointments with Flint, George C. Perkins and Knowland
Lunch with Hoke Smith and Kellogg

headline: Cortelyou's panic report
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt sees senators and congressmen, lunches with Elliott and Assistant Navy Secretary Newberry, rides, and writes Treasury Secretary Cortelyou about his report on the panic.

events.detail: Callers include Newberry, Curtis, Warren, Hepburn and Fassett
Responds to Cortelyou's report on the panic

letters.topic: His report on the financial panic

references.title: The Letters of Theodore Roosevelt, ed. Elting Morison

headline: Postal business and a walk
summary: A light Saturday: Roosevelt goes over postal matters with Postmaster General Meyer, confers with Vice President Fairbanks, and takes a walk.

headline: Aboard the Mayflower for Hampton Roads
summary: Roosevelt boards the presidential yacht Mayflower bound for the Virginia coast. Along are Edith, Ethel, Bamie and her husband Will Cowles, cabinet and navy families, his niece Corinne Robinson and Belle Hagner. Before sailing he writes Senator Warren about bullet evidence in the Brownsville affair, pushing back on Senator Foraker.

events.detail: Leaves by presidential yacht for the Virginia coast with family and guests
Letter to Senator Warren on bullets from Brownsville

letters.topic: Antimony in the Brownsville bullets, answering Foraker

uncertain: Metcalfs, Newberrys, Brownsons and Sims' are listed as couples; only the husbands are named here.

headline: The Great White Fleet sails
summary: From the deck of the Mayflower at Hampton Roads, Roosevelt speaks and then watches sixteen battleships under Rear Admiral Robley Evans steam out on a voyage around the world. The cruise is meant to show Japan the nation's resolve, build support in Congress for the Navy, and prove a whole battle fleet can circle the globe. He returns to Washington.

events.detail: Addresses the fleet before it sails
Watches the Great White Fleet depart on its world cruise

headline: Bring the troops home from Nevada
summary: With Nevada calm since the soldiers arrived, Roosevelt wires Governor Sparks that he means to pull them out soon. He also meets the Cabinet, talks Missouri appointments with Representative Bartholdt, and plays tennis.

events.detail: Telegram to Sparks about withdrawing troops

letters.topic: With Nevada quiet, he wants federal troops out quickly

headline: Why not a third term
summary: Roosevelt sees Lodge and other lawmakers and goes riding. To English writer Frederic Harrison he lays out his reasons for stepping aside after this term, and mentions the introduction he wrote for Jeremiah Curtin's The Mongols: A History.

events.detail: Callers include Lodge, Proctor, Dillingham and Underwood
Explains to Frederic Harrison his choice not to run again

letters.topic: His reasons against a third term; his preface to Curtin's Mongols

works.title: Introduction to The Mongols: A History by Jeremiah Curtin

uncertain: The record spells it 'Frederick Harrison'; this is likely the English positivist Frederic Harrison.

headline: Tonto National Monument proclaimed
summary: Roosevelt protects the cliff dwellings of Tonto in Arizona as a national monument. He sees Senators Warren, Cullom and Hale and Governor Hoggatt, plays tennis with Jusserand, Meyer and Nick Longworth, and hosts the Cabinet dinner.

events.detail: Senators, congressmen and Governor Hoggatt call
Tennis with Jusserand, Meyer and Nick Longworth

uncertain: The record gives only the surname; Governor Hoggatt is taken to be Wilford B. Hoggatt, Governor of Alaska.

headline: Troops coming out of Nevada
summary: Hearing nothing back from Governor Sparks, Roosevelt wires that he has decided to withdraw federal troops from Nevada. He also lunches with canal chief George Goethals, rides, and spends the evening with Root, Bacon and Taft.

events.detail: Evening sessions with Root, Bacon and Taft
Wires Sparks that the troops will be withdrawn

letters.topic: No reply received, so the troops will leave

headline: Central American peace delegates welcomed
summary: Roosevelt hosts the delegates to the Central American Peace Conference and talks New York politics with Herbert Parsons. He writes a long letter to Cecil Spring-Rice touching on his friend's frustration with diplomatic life, Australia, population and the panic, and tells Thomas Watson why printing greenbacks is no cure.

events.detail: New York politics with Parsons, Olcott and Merritt
Taft, Speaker Cannon and Governor Hoggatt among the callers
Reception for Central American Peace Conference delegates
Letters to Spring-Rice and Thomas Watson

letters.topic: His discouragement with diplomacy; Australia, population, the future, the panic
Why issuing greenbacks won't end the panic

headline: Taft versus Foraker in Ohio
summary: On Sunday evening Postmaster General Meyer and Secretary Root call. Roosevelt writes Arizona's Governor Kibbey about maneuvering ahead of the Republican convention, where Taft's backers are battling Foraker's.

events.detail: Letter to Governor Kibbey on convention politics

letters.topic: Taft and Foraker camps maneuvering before the national convention

headline: A grandnephew is born to Franklin and Eleanor
summary: James Roosevelt, son of Franklin and Eleanor, is born. Roosevelt sits for photographer Frederick Hyde, discusses Pacific Coast defenses with Flint and Humphrey, and lunches with Leo Rowe and Kitagaki. He tells Charles Magoon the pitcher and basin Magoon sent will be Edith's Christmas present, and asks Bonaparte about stopping union boycotts.

events.detail: James Roosevelt born to Eleanor and Franklin D. Roosevelt
Callers include Long, Burkett and Garfield
Pacific Coast fortifications with Flint and Humphrey
Lunch with Leo Rowe and Kitagaki

letters.topic: His gift of a pitcher and basin, now Edith's Christmas present
Curbing labor union boycotts

headline: Christmas tree at the German Embassy
summary: On Christmas Eve Roosevelt meets the Cabinet, talks finance with Senator Hansbrough, and stops by the German Embassy to admire its Christmas tree before tennis with Pinchot and Jusserand. He tells Root that Panama has no say at all over the waters approaching the Canal Zone.

events.detail: Separate meetings with Heney and Governor Hoggatt
Visits the German Embassy's Christmas tree
Tells Root that Panama lacks jurisdiction over canal approaches

letters.topic: Panama has no authority over the canal's approach waters

headline: Christmas at the White House
summary: At seven in the morning the children, Alice and Nick included, pile onto the bed to open stockings, then everyone heads to the library for presents. Roosevelt rides three hours with Root, Lodge, Fitz Lee, Ted, Kermit and Ethel, admires Archie's tree, and plays an hour and a half of tennis, while Quentin's three friends roughhouse all evening.

events.detail: Children open their stockings on their parents' bed
Gifts opened in the library after breakfast
Three-hour ride with family and friends
Family looks at Archie's Christmas tree
An hour and a half of tennis
Quentin's friends romp through the evening
Thanks Bamie for her gift of a lamp

letters.topic: Thanks for the lamp

headline: Off to Pine Knot for the holidays
summary: Roosevelt heads for the family's Virginia cabin, Pine Knot, stopping in Charlottesville. He protests a New York Tribune editorial claiming Admiral Brownson quit over the order putting naval doctors in command of hospital ships, and tells Arthur Lee why he won't run again and about Philip de László's wish to paint him.

events.detail: Letters to Hart Lyman and Arthur Lee

letters.topic: Objects to the Tribune's account of Brownson's resignation
No third term; de László hopes to paint his portrait

headline: At Pine Knot
summary: Roosevelt is at Pine Knot, the family's retreat in the Virginia woods. Nothing else is recorded for the day.

headline: Nevada must call its legislature
summary: From Pine Knot Roosevelt wires Governor Sparks that Nevada's legislature must be summoned at once. Keeping order is the state's job, he says, and if the call does not go out within five days the federal troops will leave.

events.detail: Telegram pressing Sparks to convene the Nevada legislature

letters.topic: Call the legislature within five days or the troops go

headline: Report on the panic arrives
summary: Roosevelt remains at Pine Knot as Treasury Secretary Cortelyou turns in his account of the autumn's financial panic.

events.detail: Cortelyou submits his report on the panic

headline: Back to Washington from Pine Knot
summary: Roosevelt leaves Pine Knot in the afternoon and has appointments that evening in Washington. He writes Alabama judge John C. Anderson to praise him for enjoining state railroad regulation laws.

letters.topic: Commends his injunctions against Alabama railroad laws

headline: Year ends as the panic eases
summary: Roosevelt closes 1907 with tennis and letters: to Taft on Ohio politics and Foraker, to Leo Rowe on ties with South America, and to Owen Wister on scholarship in America. With the economy recovering, the panic is over. Scribner's publishes his "In the Louisiana Canebrakes."

events.detail: Tennis with Pinchot, Garfield and Jusserand
Letters to Taft, Rowe and Wister
"In the Louisiana Canebrakes" appears in Scribner's Magazine
"Our National Inland Waterways Policy" appears in the Annals of the American Academy

headline: Six thousand at the New Year's reception
summary: Roosevelt opens 1908 with breakfast with Captain Greenaway, then greets some 6,000 people at the New Year's reception. That afternoon he takes a hard two-hour ride with his children and their cousins and friends, and writes Trevelyan about the inscribed loving cup and the Revolution.

Long ride with his children and their friends
Writes Trevelyan about the cup and Revolutionary history

letters.topic: The inscribed cup, Revolutionary War questions, the Rough Riders

headline: Howard Pyle comes to lunch
summary: Roosevelt names J. E. Pillsbury to head the Bureau of Navigation, tours the Corcoran early, and lunches with Taft, illustrator Howard Pyle and Eugene Philbin. He writes Archie at Groton about Edith's fondness for the little dog Scamp, and congratulates Bonaparte on a Chicago speech on the misdeeds of the rich.

events.detail: Pillsbury put in charge of the Navy's navigation bureau
Callers include Seth Bullock and Metcalf
Lunch with Pyle, Philbin and Taft
Letters to Archie, Bonaparte, Cortelyou and Metcalf

Currency
Pillsbury's appointment and friction in the Navy

headline: A musicale after dinner
summary: After the Cabinet meeting and a few callers, Roosevelt plays tennis and hosts Goethals, Rockhill, Whitelaw Reid and Beveridge at dinner, followed by music.

events.detail: Callers include Bourne, S. N. D. North and DeGraw
Tennis with Garfield, Cooley and Jusserand

headline: Doctors to command hospital ships
summary: Roosevelt hears from Charles Neill on labor conditions in Nevada and from Representative Humphrey on Puget Sound defenses, and sees Jacob Riis and Seth Bullock. headline: Seth Bullock stays over
summary: Roosevelt's old Dakota friend Seth Bullock and his wife spend Sunday night at the White House.

headline: More power for Goethals
summary: As Congress returns, Roosevelt widens the authority of Colonel Goethals as chairman of the Isthmian Canal Commission. He poses for Mr. Hyde on the South Portico, plays tennis, and writes Taft about removing federal officeholders.

events.detail: A New York City appointment with Parsons, Olcott and Bennet

Taft, Meyer and Beveridge among callers

Tennis with Cooley, Garfield and Jusserand
Letters to Taft and Matthew Hale

headline: Aldrich offers an emergency currency bill
summary: Senator Aldrich introduces a bill allowing $500 million in emergency currency when credit tightens. Roosevelt meets the Cabinet, lunches with Taft, Longworth and Seth Bullock, walks, and he and Edith dine with Vice President Fairbanks.

events.detail: Callers include Bacon and C. A. Prouty
Aldrich introduces his emergency currency bill
Midday meal with Taft, Bullock and others
The Fairbankses host the Roosevelts for dinner

headline: George Ade at the table
summary: Roosevelt confers with Payne and Dalzell, the House's tariff men, and lunches with humorist George Ade, Robert Porter and Sloan Simpson, who stays the night. After a ride he dines with Captain Lee.

events.detail: Root, Clapp and Colonel McCook among callers
Lunch with Simpson, Ade and Porter

headline: Muir Woods saved
summary: Roosevelt proclaims Muir Woods in California a national monument, protecting its redwoods. Taft and La Follette are among the day's callers, he rides at three, and that night hosts the diplomatic reception. He sends George Meredith congratulations on the novelist's 80th birthday.

events.detail: Callers include Taft and La Follette

letters.topic: Congratulations at eighty

headline: A dinner for Speaker Cannon
summary: Roosevelt sorts out Nebraska postal jobs with Senators Burkett and Brown and later hosts a dinner and musicale honoring Speaker Joe Cannon. In New York, Taft speaks at Cooper Union on the origins of property. Roosevelt thanks his brother-in-law Douglas Robinson for managing his money.

Taft addresses Cooper Union in New York

summary: Roosevelt proclaims the Grand Canyon a national monument. He discusses fortifying Pearl Harbor, the tariff and an employers' liability bill, lunches and walks with Jusserand, and writes about saving Appalachian forests, better language teaching at West Point, and his record for working people.

summary: Roosevelt goes over land fraud prosecutions with Garfield and Ballinger and sees Bonaparte and Nebraska's Senator Burkett. Tennis with Garfield, Pinchot and Jusserand

headline: A growling teddy bear from the Black Forest
summary: Roosevelt hosts a late reception for both houses of Congress. To Archie he reports that Ted hopes to finish college in three years and earn his own way, that Quentin is playing with the Turkish minister's son, and that a walking, growling black teddy bear has made Ethel jealous.

summary: Roosevelt sends Congress a special message unlike any before it: he calls for a new employers' liability law, limits on injunctions in labor disputes, federal control of stock gambling, and tighter rules for railroads and big combinations.
